findings.summary: Search query is silently dropped when credentials contain gmail.metadata scope alongside full-access scopes (e.g., gmail.readonly). The check uses membership (`in`) instead of verifying metadata is the exclusive scope.
findings.failure_scenario: GmailReadBlock with query='is:unread', max_results=5; credentials.scopes=['https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly','https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.metadata'] -> query is not added to list() kwargs, the API returns all messages unfiltered instead of only unread.

findings.summary: Message/thread format forced to 'metadata' (stripping email bodies) when gmail.metadata scope is present alongside full-access scopes. Same membership-check flaw: user has full read permission but gets empty bodies.
findings.failure_scenario: credentials.scopes=['gmail.readonly','gmail.metadata']; GmailReadBlock or GmailGetThreadBlock calls messages.get() with format='metadata' -> all message bodies return 'This email does not contain a text body.' despite the user having full gmail.readonly access that supports format='full'. Same defect exists in _get_thread at line 592.

findings.summary: _get_attachments crashes with KeyError on metadata-format messages because part['body']['attachmentId'] is absent in metadata-format API responses. The PR introduces metadata-format responses but does not guard attachment processing.
findings.failure_scenario: Message with attachments fetched with format='metadata' (triggered by the scope-check defect above); _get_attachments iterates parts, finds a part with filename=True, then accesses part['body']['attachmentId'] -> KeyError because metadata-format body dicts only contain 'size', not 'attachmentId'. Same defect in GmailGetThreadBlock._get_attachments at line 658.
